tagline: Hundreds of boats run the same four lagoon loops every single morning — the textbook captive day-loop mesh for clean foiling.
summary: El Nido's Bacuit Bay is the most standardized boat-tour market in Southeast Asia: the LGU packages the entire archipelago into four fixed loops (Tours A, B, C and D), and a diesel bangka fleet runs them daily for a visitor flow that has overshot the town's assessed carrying capacity (~600,000 arrivals against ~400,000). Fixed routes, fixed stops, daily-capped lagoons inside a managed protected area — predictable duty cycles, short legs, and a regulator actively looking for lower-impact operations make this the natural home for a quiet, zero-emission, wake-free foiling fleet.

use_cases.title: Electrify the Tour A–D loops
use_cases.body: The four standardized lagoon-and-island loops are short-leg, fixed-route, daily-repeat — a perfect all-electric duty cycle. Foiling tour craft cut noise, fumes and wake inside the lagoons that the daily caps exist to protect, and lift throughput per permitted slot with faster inter-stop legs.

use_cases.title: Resort-island shuttle network
use_cases.body: Miniloc, Lagen and Pangulasian (El Nido Resorts) plus the Lio (Ayala) beachfront sit 2–6 nm apart. Silent foiling transfers between Lio Beach Pier, town and the island resorts turn every guest movement into a signature experience inside the protected bay.

use_cases.title: Lio / Corong-Corong gateway circulation
use_cases.body: Arrivals flow through Lio airport and the Corong-Corong bangka landings south of town. A scheduled foiling shuttle (with the 12–15-pax N35 Shuttle from 2027 as the native scheduled platform) organizes the gateway-to-bay flow that today scatters across beach-launched bancas.

use_cases.title: El Nido ↔ Coron line-haul
use_cases.body: The signature northern-Palawan crossing (~73 nm routed past Linapacan) is a notorious multi-hour, swell-exposed fastcraft run today. Just beyond the all-electric envelope, it is a natural early Quanta-LR hybrid corridor from H2 2026+ — no charging infrastructure needed at either end.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Bacuit Bay is a compact 0–10 nm mesh — the Tour A–D loops, the Lio↔town gateway spine and the Miniloc/Lagen/Pangulasian resort triangle all run deep inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with many rotations per charge. The ~63 nm run south to Sabang (Underground River) fits but is near the range edge and flagged for coordinate-level confirmation before scheduling.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: El Nido ↔ Coron (~73 nm routed) is just past the electric envelope — a natural first Quanta-LR hybrid corridor from H2 2026+ — and Cebu ↔ El Nido (~271 nm) connects Bacuit Bay to the Visayas mesh with no destination charging dependency. Coron and Amanpulo are covered in the adjacent Palawan brief; cross-linked, not duplicated.

competitive_landscape: The bay is served by the LGU-organized bangka tour fleet running Tours A–D (cooperative-operated, hundreds of daily departures), El Nido Resorts' own transfer boats, fastcraft operators on the El Nido↔Coron crossing, and 5–6-hour vans from Puerto Princesa. The demand is proven, standardized and capacity-rationed — the rare market where the regulator, the resort anchor and the visitor all want the same thing: fewer fumes, less wake, less noise, and reliability in swell. The status quo fleet can deliver none of those.
seasonality: Amihan (Nov–May) is the calm, dry peak across Bacuit Bay; habagat (Jun–Oct) brings southwest swell, rain and frequent tour cancellations — the window where foiling above the chop converts cancelled days into operating days. Northern Palawan sits on the typhoon belt's fringe; statutory PAGASA signal closures apply during named storms.
regulatory_note: El Nido waters fall under the El Nido–Taytay Managed Resource Protected Area and Palawan's ECAN zoning regime (SEP Act, RA 7611) administered through the PCSD — environmentally tiered use is the law of the bay, not a guideline. The LGU already enforces tour-loop standardization, carrying-capacity studies and daily site caps, and is publicly seeking lower-impact operations. Vessel certification through MARINA; access via El Nido Ferry Terminal, Lio Beach Pier and the Corong-Corong landings.

precedents.where: Maldives (with JIH Global), first 5 vessels in 2026, 3-year phased rollout
precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that protected-water, resort-anchored archipelagos adopt clean foiling at fleet scale — Bacuit Bay's standardized loops are an even tighter operational fit.
Philippine authorities demonstrably act on environmental carrying capacity at flagship destinations — El Nido's own caps follow the same playbook, rewarding operators who get ahead of it.
